leading_positions.synthesis: Six of the eight round-1 files name B029 (Katori and Ye) as the preferred configuration. All six give the same two laureates, and all cite the same core merits: magic-wavelength trapping as the single originating idea, realisation at the 10^-18 level, reproduction at several independent laboratories, and concrete uses in tests of constants and relativistic geodesy. They are not identical on the citation. Kroll and Olsson write new tests of fundamental physics into the wording, Kroll also mentions a path to redefining the second, while Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce confine it to the invention and the demonstrated precision, and several explicitly do not want the pending redefinition of the second to carry the case. Johansson, Mehlig and Pearce moved to B029 after reading the opening ballots (from B018, B039 and B013 respectively). All six also state the same main reservation, overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and agree that other clock groups are outside the two names. They differ on how serious that is.

Danielsson alone prefers the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson, credited to Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee as founders and long-time leaders of ATLAS and CMS. He argues that it is the clearest concrete discovery on the shortlist, that it was independently established by two experiments, that its properties have held up, and that the experimental side is overdue after the 2013 theory prize. He acknowledges that the three-name set is contestable and that he relies on general knowledge of founding roles. Colleagues who answer him (Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig, Pearce) do not dispute the importance or maturity of the science. They object that the citation rewards conception and construction leadership more than the discovery analysis, and that no stated principle selects three people from two collaborations of several thousand.

Eriksson alone prefers dynamical mean-field theory (Georges, Vollhardt, Kotliar), arguing it is the strongest case on originality, durability and breadth, and a standard route to correlated materials through DFT+DMFT. He states that no one else has it in their top four and that he does not claim broad support. He names Metzner's omission and the limits of single-site DMFT in low dimensions as real weaknesses. Colleagues who comment (Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig) accept the conceptual weight but treat the Metzner attribution gap as the deciding difficulty. Eriksson says he now regards his own ranking of B029 as too low and would support it as a prize.

areas_of_agreement: Every member who commented on B029 accepts that it is a well-bounded invention with a clear originating idea (magic-wavelength trapping) and a record-precision demonstration, and that performance at 10^-18 has been reproduced and intercompared across independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN and Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST).
Every member who proposes laureates for B029 gives the same two names, Katori and Ye, so no disagreement about the credited pair arises inside the committee.

Nobody disputes the scientific importance or maturity of the Higgs discovery (B012). The objections from Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig and Pearce concern the attribution of three names, not the science.

Several members, including Johansson, Lindroth and Pearce, would not let the pending redefinition of the second serve as the merit of a B029 prize. Kroll says explicitly that he is not arguing from it.

Members who discuss B018 (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce, Eriksson) agree that the Cirac-Zoller proposal is conceptually important and that its standing depends on the overlap with the 2012 prize and on experimental credit beyond Blatt.
scientific_disputes: Is the optical lattice clock a distinct step or a continuation of recognised work? Hall and Haensch (2005, frequency comb as readout) and Wineland and Haroche (2012, ion control, including Al+ ion clocks) are cited by the supporters themselves as the main reservation. Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce argue the lattice scheme (many neutral atoms, Doppler- and recoil-free) is a separate achievement and treat ion clocks as sibling work. Eriksson and Mehlig put more weight on the comparison, and Eriksson regards DMFT as the more fundamental new idea.

For B018, how much is new beyond the 2012 prize? Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Eriksson and Pearce raise this, and Eriksson would want the committee to say precisely what is new beyond Wineland and Haroche. Johansson places B018 behind the clocks for this reason, but Kroll lists it as his first alternative.

B031 is the most frequent alternative to B029 in the files (Danielsson, Eriksson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson). Eriksson and Danielsson say the origin of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated, which bears on whether the field is ready. Lindroth values that the prediction preceded the measurement.

Whether the demonstrated performance or the prospective physics should anchor the B029 citation. Pearce notes that nobody has yet used the clocks to find a violation of a fundamental constant, and Kroll and Olsson include new tests of fundamental physics in their wording.

Pearce's own B013 and B037 are not in any colleague's preferred configuration. Pearce moved off B013 in round 1, while Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson reply that they see credit gaps in them. The files give no one's view on whether the discovery merit of B013 has been heard fully.
attribution_disputes: B012: whether Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee can fairly stand for ATLAS and CMS. Danielsson concedes that spokespersons at the time of discovery, detector pioneers and accelerator leaders have comparable claims. Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig and Pearce ask what principle selects three people, and Eriksson would need a decisive individual contribution argued explicitly.

B035: Metzner's infinite-dimension contribution and the work of Mueller-Hartmann, Jarrell and Rozenberg fall outside any three-name prize. Eriksson, the proponent, calls this a real gap, and Johansson, Lindroth and Mehlig press the point.

B029: Lemonde, Ludlow, Lisdat, Hinkley, Bloom, Schiller and the Yb lattice and Al+ ion-clock groups reached comparable accuracy. Kroll, Lindroth and Mehlig suggest the citation name the lattice-clock concept and its realisation, not a record number that several groups hold.
B018: Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson note that the first ion-trap gate demonstrations came from NIST and Monroe, who are outside the credited trio.
B004: Johansson and Lindroth chose different triples from the same five-person proposal (Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf, Wallraff). Johansson treats that as showing the allocation is unresolved.

B013: Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson note that Jan van Paradijs and the optical-identification teams are not among the credited names, a point Pearce raised himself. B037: Lindroth and Mehlig object to a single name for a large collaboration.
maturity_disputes: B029 is described as mature by its supporters because of multi-laboratory reproduction. The redefinition of the second has not happened, and Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce disagree on whether waiting is a scientific criterion. Lindroth does not treat it as one.

B031: Danielsson and Eriksson say the superconducting mechanism and correlated states are unsettled and early experimental co-authors (Cao, Fatemi) are outside the credited set. Lindroth and Eriksson agree the theory preceded the experiment.

B018 and B004: Pearce and Johansson note that the competition among qubit platforms is open and that the 2025 prize on circuits reduces room for a second quantum-hardware prize soon. Olsson would defer B018 to a later year.
B037: Danielsson and Mehlig, citing Pearce's own statement, say source identification beyond the diffuse flux is statistically modest and still awaits independent confirmation.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Pearce (Chair): documented connections to PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur, and a KTH gamma-ray polarimetry programme aimed at gamma-ray bursts. He declares an interest in B013 and would stay out of the final decision on it if it advanced. He has a CERN-trained experimental background that bears on B012. He sees no specific conflict for B029.

Kroll: a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder. Jun Ye's career is tied to the Hall and JILA environment, and Kroll flags this as a perceived connection for the committee to judge. He claims no direct collaboration, supervision or shared funding with Ye or Katori. He also has field-level proximity to AMO candidates B018, B004 and B044. Mehlig and Olsson ask that the disclosure be recorded and Olsson asks that it be weighed against Lindroth's independent first-place support.

Johansson: directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and works on superconducting circuits and waveguide QED, close to B004 and to a lesser extent B018. He would recuse himself from any deliberation turning on B004. He records no link to Katori, Ye or the optical clock community.

Eriksson: uses DFT+DMFT in his own research and is a potential beneficiary of B035. B031 is also close to his field. He chaired the committee for the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, which bears on B004. He notes no specific recusal conflict.

Lindroth: long-running collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and with Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zurich. Andreas Wallraff (B004) is at ETH Zurich, institutional proximity without a documented personal tie. This does not concern her preferred configuration.
Olsson: notes that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague and says she weighs his view on its merits. Her professional proximity to materials and electron microscopy touches B010 more than B029.

Mehlig: no specific conflict. He notes intellectual proximity, not a personal tie, between his earlier first choice B039 and his field of statistical physics of disordered systems. Danielsson: no specific conflict apparent.
questions_for_round2: Do the 2005 prize (frequency comb) and the 2012 prize (control of single quantum systems, including ion clocks) leave the optical lattice clock as a separate achievement? If so, can the citation say so in a way that rests on magic-wavelength trapping and the realisation of many-atom lattice clocks?

Should the B029 citation be built on demonstrated 10^-18 performance and independent intercomparisons only, or may it refer to tests of fundamental constants and the redefinition of the second? Kroll and Olsson include new tests of fundamental physics, and Johansson, Lindroth and Pearce would not rest it on future outcomes.

Can the committee set out why Katori and Ye, and not Lemonde, Ludlow, Lisdat or the Yb and Al+ ion-clock groups, are the credited pair? Would any change to the two-name set alter the preferred configuration of any supporter?

Should Kroll's Hall-laboratory connection be treated as requiring recusal on B029, or as a disclosure only? Does the outcome change if Kroll's view is excluded, given that Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce independently prefer B029?

For B012, what principle, if any, selects three individuals from ATLAS and CMS? Can Danielsson state who made the decisive individual contribution and why spokespersons at the time of discovery and accelerator leaders are not credited, and would Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig or Pearce reconsider if he can?
For B035, can Eriksson say whether Metzner's omission is resolvable within three names (for example by redefining the citation), or does it disqualify the configuration as drafted?

If B029 does not hold, which fallback does the committee prefer: B018 (named by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce), B031 (Danielsson, Eriksson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson), or another candidate? What would each need to resolve first (Wineland overlap and NIST and Monroe credit for B018, the mechanism and credit for B031)?

Does any member wish to re-open B013, B037, B010 or B039 as preferred candidates, or are these left to later years? Pearce asks whether B013 deserves a hearing, given that colleagues object mainly on credit, and would stay out of any final decision on it.
summary.chair_observation: After one round, six of eight members name the same single prize part, B029 with the same two laureates, while the other two preferred configurations (B012 and B035) are held by one member each and are mainly contested on attribution, not on merit. The shared reservation is overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and round 2 should focus on that, on the exact citation wording, and on the treatment of Kroll's disclosure. The chair holds B029 as his own preferred configuration and moved to it after the opening ballots, so he asks the others to test it as hard as they would test any other case.
